title: Extending a morphism of the middle terms to distinguished triangles; uniqueness when Hom(X[1],Z')=0
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category] and let $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{d}X[1]$ and $X'\xrightarrow{u'}Y'\xrightarrow{v'}Z'\xrightarrow{d'}X'[1]$ be distinguished triangles, and $g:Y\to Y'$ a morphism. (1) The following are equivalent: (a) $v'gu=0$; (b) there is $f:X\to X'$ with $u'f=gu$; (b') there is $h:Z\to Z'$ with $hv=v'g$; (c) there are $f,h$ such that $(f,g,h)$ is a morphism of triangles. (2) If moreover $\Hom_{\mathcal T}(X[1],Z')=0$, then the $f$ of (b) and the $h$ of (b') are unique; consequently, for any $f$ with $u'f=gu$ and any $h$ with $hv=v'g$, $(f,g,h)$ is a morphism of triangles, i.e. also $d'h=f[1]d$. (3) In particular, if $\Hom_{\mathcal T}(X[1],Z)=0$, then $d$ is the unique morphism $x:Z\to X[1]$ such that $X\xrightarrow{u}Y\xrightarrow{v}Z\xrightarrow{x}X[1]$ is distinguished.

source.place: Beilinson-Bernstein-Deligne, Faisceaux pervers, Proposition 1.1.9 (pp. 23-24, pdf pages 24-25) and Corollaire 1.1.10 (ii) (p. 24, pdf page 25); BBD write Hom^{-1}(X,Z') = Hom(X,Z'[-1]), isomorphic through the shift to Hom(X[1],Z'); cf. literature/stacks-project/derived.tex Lemmas 0146 and 0149 (lines 358, 386) for the exact Hom sequences used in the proof

proof.text: **Step 1 ((a) ⇒ (b)).** Suppose $v'gu=0$. The morphism $gu:X\to Y'$ satisfies $v'\circ(gu)=0$, so by the exactness of $\Hom(X,X')\to\Hom(X,Y')\to\Hom(X,Z')$ ([lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] (ii), applied to the triangle $(X',Y',Z',u',v',d')$ with $W=X$) there is $f:X\to X'$ with $gu=u'f$, i.e. the square (1) commutes.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and its proof, pp. 23-24 (pdf pages 24-25): 'L'exactitude de la suite Hom^{-1}(X,Z') → Hom(X,X') → Hom(X,Y') → Hom(X,Z'), appliquée à gu, montre que (a) ⇔ (b)'

proof.text: **Step 2 ((b) ⇒ (c)).** If $f$ satisfies $u'f=gu$, axiom TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] (BBD call it TR 2 here) applied to the two distinguished triangles and the pair $(f,g)$ gives $h:Z\to Z'$ with $hv=v'g$ and $f[1]\circ d=d'\circ h$, so $(f,g,h)$ is a morphism of triangles [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift].

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and its proof, pp. 23-24 (pdf pages 24-25): 'Que (b) ⇒ (c) résulte de TR 2'

proof.text: **Step 3 ((c) ⇒ (b), (c) ⇒ (b'), (b) ⇒ (a)).** A morphism of triangles $(f,g,h)$ [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift] has $u'f=gu$ and $hv=v'g$ among its conditions, so (c) gives (b) and (b'). If $u'f=gu$, then $v'gu=v'u'f=0$ because $v'u'=0$ ([lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] (i) for the triangle $(X',Y',Z',u',v',d')$).

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and its proof, pp. 23-24 (pdf pages 24-25): 'La réciproque est triviale'; (b) ⇒ (a) is the other half of the exactness used in Step 1

proof.text: **Step 4 ((a) ⇒ (b')).** Suppose $v'gu=0$. The morphism $v'g:Y\to Z'$ satisfies $(v'g)\circ u=0$, so by the exactness of $\Hom(Z,Z')\to\Hom(Y,Z')\to\Hom(X,Z')$ ([lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] (i), applied to the triangle $(X,Y,Z,u,v,d)$ with $W=Z'$) there is $h:Z\to Z'$ with $v'g=hv$, i.e. the square (2) commutes.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, proof, p. 24 (pdf page 25): 'Enfin, un argument dual fournit (a) ⇔ (b')'

proof.text: **Step 5 ((b′) ⇒ (a)).** If T.mor₂ ≫ h = g ≫ T′.mor₂, then T.mor₁ ≫ g ≫ T′.mor₂ = T.mor₁ ≫ T.mor₂ ≫ h = 0 by comp_distTriang_mor_zero₁₂. With Steps 1–4, this proves the three equivalences. No second-square TR3 lemma is needed.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, proof, p. 24 (pdf page 25): 'un argument dual fournit (a) ⇔ (b')'

proof.text: **Step 6 (uniqueness of $f$ in (2)).** Suppose $\Hom(X[1],Z')=0$ and $f_1,f_2:X\to X'$ both satisfy $u'f_i=gu$. Put $e=f_1-f_2$ (the category is additive); then $u'e=0$. The shift $[1]$ is an additive functor, so $u'[1]\circ e[1]=(u'e)[1]=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] (iii) for the triangle $(X',Y',Z',u',v',d')$ with $W=X[1]$ there is $k:X[1]\to Z'$ with $e[1]=d'\circ k$; since $\Hom(X[1],Z')=0$, $k=0$ and $e[1]=0$. As $[1]$ is an automorphism (an auto-equivalence suffices) of $\mathcal T$ [def-weil-triangulated-category], it is faithful, so $e=0$, i.e. $f_1=f_2$. (BBD state the hypothesis as $\Hom^{-1}(X,Z')=\Hom(X,Z'[-1])=0$ and use the exact sequence $\Hom(X,Z'[-1])\to\Hom(X,X')\to\Hom(X,Y')$; the shift $[1]$ identifies it with $\Hom(X[1],Z')\to\Hom(X[1],X'[1])\to\Hom(X[1],Y'[1])$ used here.) In Lean this is the already proved source-library Triangle.cancel_mor₁_of_subsingleton, whose proof uses coyoneda_exact₁ and faithfulness of shift.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and its proof, pp. 23-24 (pdf pages 24-25): '... avec unicité de f si Hom^{-1}(X,Z') = 0'

proof.text: **Step 7 (uniqueness of $h$ in (2)).** Suppose $\Hom(X[1],Z')=0$ and $h_1,h_2:Z\to Z'$ both satisfy $h_iv=v'g$. Put $e=h_1-h_2$; then $ev=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact] (ii) for the triangle $(X,Y,Z,u,v,d)$ with $W=Z'$ there is $k:X[1]\to Z'$ with $e=k\circ d$; since $\Hom(X[1],Z')=0$, $k=0$, so $e=0$ and $h_1=h_2$. In Lean this is the already proved source-library Triangle.cancel_mor₂_of_subsingleton, whose proof uses yoneda_exact₃.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, proof, p. 24 (pdf page 25): '... et l'unicité de h si Hom^{-1}(X,Z') = 0' (the dual exact sequence Hom(X[1],Z') → Hom(Z,Z') → Hom(Y,Z'))

proof.text: **Step 8 (any such $f$, $h$ form a morphism of triangles).** Suppose $\Hom(X[1],Z')=0$, $u'f=gu$ and $hv=v'g$. By Step 2 (TR3 of [def-weil-triangulated-category] applied to $(f,g)$) there is $h_0$ with $(f,g,h_0)$ a morphism of triangles; $h_0v=v'g$, so $h_0=h$ by Step 7. Hence $(f,g,h)$ is a morphism of triangles [def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift]; in particular $d'\circ h=f[1]\circ d$. This finishes part (2).

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, last sentence of the statement, p. 23 (pdf page 24), with Steps 2 and 7

proof.text: **Step 9 (part (3): uniqueness of the third arrow).** Let $\Hom(X[1],Z)=0$ and let $x:Z\to X[1]$ be such that $(X,Y,Z,u,v,x)$ is distinguished. Apply part (2) to the triangles $(X,Y,Z,u,v,d)$ and $(X',Y',Z',u',v',d')=(X,Y,Z,u,v,x)$ with $g=\mathrm{id}_Y$; here $\Hom(X[1],Z')=\Hom(X[1],Z)=0$. The morphisms $f=\mathrm{id}_X$ and $h=\mathrm{id}_Z$ satisfy $u\circ\mathrm{id}_X=\mathrm{id}_Y\circ u$ and $\mathrm{id}_Z\circ v=v\circ\mathrm{id}_Y$, so by Step 8 $(\mathrm{id}_X,\mathrm{id}_Y,\mathrm{id}_Z)$ is a morphism of triangles, and its third square reads $x\circ\mathrm{id}_Z=\mathrm{id}_X[1]\circ d$. Since $[1]$ is a functor, $\mathrm{id}_X[1]=\mathrm{id}_{X[1]}$, hence $x=d$. Conversely $d$ itself has the property, so $d$ is the unique such morphism. The Lean proof directly applies complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism with identity first and middle components, identifies its third component c with the identity by Triangle.cancel_mor₂_of_subsingleton, and simplifies the last square.

source.place: Corollaire 1.1.10 (ii) and its proof, p. 24 (pdf page 25): 'Pour (ii), on applique 1.1.9 à (X,Y,Z,u,v,d) et (X,Y,Z,u,v,x). On a nécessairement h = Id_Z, d'où d = x'

proof_origin.place: Proposition 1.1.9 and its proof (pp. 23-24, pdf pages 24-25), Corollaire 1.1.10 (ii) and its proof (p. 24, pdf page 25)

split_report.summary: Read BBD 1.1.9-1.1.10 (pdftotext, pdf pages 24-25; the node's place said p. 23 for both, corrected: 1.1.9 runs over pp. 23-24, 1.1.10 is on p. 24). The statement agrees with BBD (Hom^{-1}(X,Z') of BBD = Hom(X,Z'[-1]) ≅ Hom(X[1],Z')) and is kept; morphism of triangles now cites def-weil-pbc-triangles-with-shift in stmt_deps. Not a Mathlib leaf: Mathlib has the ingredients but no lemma for the uniqueness clauses (2), (3) (TStructure.triangle_map_ext/triangle_map_exists in TStructure/TruncLTGE.lean:52,71 are the t-structure special case with Hom vanishing coming from t-degrees, not the general Hom(X[1],Z')=0 statement). Proof written in 9 steps from BBD's proof: (1) through the exact Hom sequences and TR3, (2) uniqueness of f via Hom(X[1],-) applied to the second triangle and faithfulness of the shift, uniqueness of h via Hom(-,Z') applied to the first, the morphism property from TR3 plus uniqueness, (3) from (2) with g = id. Three new Mathlib leaves, each one Mathlib lemma per clause: lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact (comp_distTriang_mor_zero₁₂, Triangle.coyoneda_exact₂, Triangle.coyoneda_exact₁), lem-weil-pbc-hom-out-of-triangle-exact (Triangle.yoneda_exact₂, yoneda_exact₃), lem-weil-pbc-tr3-second-square (complete_distinguished_triangle_morphism₁); TR3 itself is in the Mathlib leaf def-weil-triangulated-category.

lean.statement: theorem triangle_morphism_extension {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Preadditive C] [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C] (T T' : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C) (hT' : T' ∈ distTriang C) (g : T.obj₂ ⟶ T'.obj₂) : ((T.mor₁ ≫ g ≫ T'.mor₂ = 0 ↔ ∃ f : T.obj₁ ⟶ T'.obj₁, f ≫ T'.mor₁ = T.mor₁ ≫ g) ∧ (T.mor₁ ≫ g ≫ T'.mor₂ = 0 ↔ ∃ h : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₃, T.mor₂ ≫ h = g ≫ T'.mor₂) ∧ (T.mor₁ ≫ g ≫ T'.mor₂ = 0 ↔ ∃ τ : T ⟶ T', τ.hom₂ = g)) ∧ (Subsingleton (T.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ T'.obj₃) → (∀ (f₁ f₂ : T.obj₁ ⟶ T'.obj₁), f₁ ≫ T'.mor₁ = T.mor₁ ≫ g → f₂ ≫ T'.mor₁ = T.mor₁ ≫ g → f₁ = f₂) ∧ (∀ (h₁ h₂ : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₃), T.mor₂ ≫ h₁ = g ≫ T'.mor₂ → T.mor₂ ≫ h₂ = g ≫ T'.mor₂ → h₁ = h₂) ∧ (∀ (f : T.obj₁ ⟶ T'.obj₁) (h : T.obj₃ ⟶ T'.obj₃), f ≫ T'.mor₁ = T.mor₁ ≫ g → T.mor₂ ≫ h = g ≫ T'.mor₂ → ∃ τ : T ⟶ T', τ.hom₁ = f ∧ τ.hom₂ = g ∧ τ.hom₃ = h ∧ T.mor₃ ≫ f⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧' = h ≫ T'.mor₃)) ∧ (Subsingleton (T.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧ ⟶ T.obj₃) → ∀ (x : T.obj₃ ⟶ T.obj₁⟦(1 : ℤ)⟧), Triangle.mk T.mor₁ T.mor₂ x ∈ distTriang C → x = T.mor₃)
